newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian PM pledges aid for cyclone-hit Bangladesh.
newsitem.headline: Indian PM pledges aid for cyclone-hit Bangladesh.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral expressed anguish on Tuesday over the deaths of hundreds of people in a cyclone that pounded Bangladesh, and said New Delhi was rushing emergency aid to its neighbour.

"I learnt with anguish and sorrow of the terrible cyclone which has devastated parts of coastal Bangladesh with large scale loss of life and destruction of property," Gujral said in a letter to Bangladesh's Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina.
"The people of India share your grief and sorrow on this occasion."
"I am directing officials in my government to rush emergency supplies to Bangladesh as our contribution for the relief efforts which your government is putting in place," Gujral said.
No detail or amount was mentioned.
Bangladesh on Tuesday launched a massive rescue and relief operation in areas devastated by high winds and tidal waves.

The government-run Bangladesh Times reported that up to 500 people were feared dead. Other newspapers, quoting their own sources, put the death toll at more than 350, and said than 2,000 people were injured in the port city of Chittagong.
The known death toll so far was 95, government officials said.
Bangladesh's worst cyclone in 1991 killed 138,000 people and left millions homeless.
